questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country were native english, so I would be able to understand the lectures to the fullest and make friends, that was not only other international students, but be a part of the everyday life by not having a language gap. The selection of courses at the university were also crucial.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There was always the opportunity to write an email to the exchange office at KU or UCC, who would replied quickly and guide you to the information you were seeking.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails from the hosting university, two orientation days, guided tour at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy, but expensive, so I would not recommend it do to the prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I did not meet anyone living on campus, so it was fine and normal to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offer you the most expensive housing, so if you have the energy, search on your own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got an email from my host institution, where I had to send my grades, and fill a form. Then later in the progress I send my wishes for courses and the acceptance from my home institution of the classes I wanted to take. Upon arrival I signed up for the classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email to Erasmus coordinator, student center, learning center, professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, so very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go for the classes you want to explore. Exchange is about both the social, the new culture, the classes, so even if the class disappoints, you will still learn a lot from it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had classes on all 3 levels; 1st year, 2nd year and 3rd year classes. The level was high academic english in the 2nd and 3rd year classes, where the 1st year classes was really high level in understanding academic theories in the culture you are in.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The host institution more lectures than seminars, where at UCPH I am use to seminars, discussion groups and interacting with the teacher a lot. There was less of that at my host institution, but there was still a lot of answering question and still having a debate with the teacher and fellow students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 'Social Analysis', 'Contemporary Criminological Theory', 'Political Sociology', and 'Family, Gender, Sexualities'

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
'Social Analysis' was super interesting, as it combined the everyday life and practice in Ireland with some of the bigger sociological theories from Marx, Foucault, Weber, Bourdieu, etc. Very interesting to get the irish point of view through this course. 
'Family, Gender, Sexualities' were also a great course, as it was very interactive between students and teacher and a lot of different people were in the class from a lot of different countries (still mainly irish people, but definitely a more diverse class).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Traveling and social meetings. I spend a lot of money traviling around in my host country, on tourist attraction, busses, trains. Besides that there was meeting with friends, which then often included buying food in town and not cooking yourself, drinking coffee while studying, etc. 
Laundry cost 30 DKK and drying 15 DKK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Laundry and drying was a lot more expensive than I expected. Drinks were a lot more expensive. Housing was so much more expensive than expected. Busses were super cheap (5 DKK for students).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything. Swimmingpool with steam room and sauna, three different kinds of gyms (cardio, strength, etc.), climbing wall for mountaineering, sports arena to play badminton, football, handball, squash, yoga. Outdoor athletic stadium, football fields, literally everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mountaineering club (climbing wall activities), trampolining (with personal coached that helps you), the swimming pool and the gym, be a part of the international group in Cork (they arranged meetings, and where most people met each other).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to new citys like Galway, Dublin, Belfast and explore, spend the money you will not regret it. Take the bus to beaches in Cork County, do the touristy things in Cork, because they are super nice. Go to the national parks, the nature is spectacular.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The most friendly people on earth.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do not hold back or be afraid that you have an accent that sounds wierd, they do not care, they are interested in you and why you chose to come to their city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They drive on the left side of the street.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness, and kind-hearted people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Explore the nature, it is so beautiful. Be open towards anyone you meet. Just go say hi to knew people, I promise they will not find it wierd.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the library for studying, it is a very good atmosphere to get into writing mode.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I gained.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The expenses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
